contract: doc/r38_stage1_tasks_and_acceptance.md S1-02; events are defined in spec/r3_counters.json
note: The ONE list of device counters readable through transport op 7 (PERF_READ). tools/r38/gen_counters.py generates rtl/tnca_perf_sel.vh from it, and the runtime reads names from it, so the index a host asks for and the counter the RTL returns cannot drift apart. Every counter is 64 bits, clears on rst_n only, and wraps (spec/r3_counters.json).

counters.name: perf_mem_rd_beats
counters.event: one per core read or atomic request accepted on the data port; host transfers are not counted

counters.name: perf_mem_wr_beats
counters.event: one per core write request accepted on the data port; host transfers are not counted

identities.exclusive_sum: sum of stall_exclusive == perf_stall_total over any window (by construction in tnca_core)
identities.retired: delta perf_issued over one launch == done_retired of that launch
identities.cycles_vs_done: 0 <= done_cycles + run_window_slack - delta perf_cycles. perf_cycles counts every cycle a role context runs; done_cycles counts only the shell's S_RUN window, which starts run_window_slack cycles after the core starts (S_PULSE, then SETTLE_CYCLES = 2 of S_SETTLE) and ends when the core is idle, i.e. after outstanding memory and writeback drain. The difference is therefore the drain.
identities.drain_cycles: done_cycles + run_window_slack - delta perf_cycles: cycles after the last role stopped until the core reported idle
